answer: New identities enter through a queue: the first from a funding cluster waits 24 hours, the second 72, the third 168, and each posts a 20 POA deposit locked for 30 days, forfeited on proven duplication. Like a beacon guiding ships, the queue admits one cluster identity at a time, so an attacker cannot rush 100 fakes through an inlet at once; each extra fake adds a longer wait and another 20 POA locked, so cost grows with both time and capital. That is no fable of free entry: onboarding logs, deposits and forfeiture proofs sit on-chain for public audit of every lock and wait.
